**About the Organization**

Founded in 1970, the Pride Center of the Capital Region is the oldest continuously operating LGBTQIA\+ community center in the United States. Based at 332 Hudson Avenue in Albany, New York, the Center serves a ten\-county region and exists to promote the well\-being of all lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, intersex, asexual, Two\-Spirit, and other gender\- and sexually diverse people, and those affected by discrimination based on gender identity and expression.

The Center provides direct services, education, training, community space, and advocacy, and produces Capital Pride and related signature events. The organization is committed to creating safe, affirming spaces; advancing equity and justice; and remaining a trusted, leading resource for LGBTQIA\+ and allied communities across the Capital Region, including rural and suburban communities.

**The Opportunity**

The Pride Center of the Capital Region seeks a full\-time Executive Director. The Executive Director serves as Chief Executive Officer and leads the Center in meeting organizational goals within the framework set forth by the mission statement and bylaws.

The successful candidate will possess strong leadership skills; a clear and inclusive vision for the local LGBTQIA\+ community; and strong organizational, community\-building, advocacy, and proactive outreach skills. The Executive Director will proactively engage and build trusting relationships with community members and partner organizations, conduct ongoing needs assessment and listening efforts, and translate those needs into the design and implementation of high\-quality programs, advocacy initiatives, and support systems that reflect and respond to community priorities across the Capital Region.

The Executive Director will plan and implement a successful development strategy ensuring the long\-term growth and stability of the Center, promote the organization and its mission, and serve as an ambassador and advocate in the communities it serves. This role centers equity and advocacy, with an intentional focus on improving the quality, reach, and accessibility of services for historically marginalized communities, including communities of color and transgender and gender\-diverse people.

**Compensation and Benefits**

* Annual salary: $85,000 to $90,000, commensurate with qualifications and experience.
* Flexible schedule.
* Generous paid time off.
* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* Life insurance.
* Full\-time, exempt position.

**Qualifications at a Glance**

Demonstrated experience in the nonprofit sector, including a minimum of three years in a senior management role. The successful candidate will bring demonstrated experience in public speaking, fundraising, and team leadership, with the ability to represent the Center effectively to diverse stakeholders. Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and operational accuracy are essential, along with excellent interpersonal and strategic problem\-solving abilities. Demonstrated experience working with LGBTQIA\+ communities is required. Knowledge of the greater Capital Region is an asset but is not required.

**How to Apply**

Electronic submission of application materials is preferred in Word or PDF format. **Please send a letter of interest, current resume, and salary expectations.**

The Pride Center of the Capital Region is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace that reflects the full diversity of the communities it serves. Applications are strongly encouraged from individuals of all backgrounds, particularly those from historically marginalized and underrepresented communities.

United Way of the Plains’ mission is “To improves lives by harnessing the caring power of our community to advance the common good in south central Kansas”. We bring individuals and organizations together to meet the biggest needs in our community in innovative ways. We do this by forging unlikely partnerships, forming new solutions to old problems and mobilizing the best ideas and resources. But we don’t do it alone. We inspire others to join the fight. new_jobs.title: Youth Program Director | East Triangle YMCA
new_jobs.description:
**POSITION SUMMARY:**



The Youth Program Director is responsible for leading and growing programs that reflect the YMCA’s mission and serve community needs. This role includes supervising and developing part\-time staff and volunteers, managing program operations and budgets, and ensuring a positive and high\-quality experience for participants. The Youth Program Director also builds partnerships with community organizations and supports outreach, marketing, and fundraising initiatives to strengthen engagement and impact.

  

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**


**Program Leadership**


* Maintain consistent daily presence in programs to support quality, safety, and staff oversight, following association\-specific expectations for direct service coverage and onsite visitation.
* Launch new programs and grow existing ones in alignment with strategic goals and participant interests.
* Coordinate facility use and logistics to support smooth program delivery and engaging events.
* Manage daily participant records by using program software to track attendance and verify and track essential information.


**Staff Development**


* Recruit, train, schedule, and support part\-time staff and volunteers to build a strong, inclusive team.
* Provide regular feedback and coaching to help staff grow and succeed.
* Motivate your team to meet goals and create a positive, mission\-driven work culture.


**Community Engagement \& Outreach**


* Build partnerships with schools, nonprofits, and other organizations to strengthen program impact and visibility.
* Support outreach, marketing, and registration efforts to promote programs and ensure access for all.


**Fiscal Stewardship**


* Develop and manage program budgets to meet financial goals and use resources responsibly.
* Contribute to the YMCA Annual Campaign by leading volunteer teams, supporting fundraising events, and achieving an individual fundraising goal that advances the branch’s overall target.


**Program Experience**


* Build strong relationships with members, families, and staff through positive, responsive communication.
* Address questions and concerns in a timely and professional manner.
* Track program data to evaluate success, improve experiences, and celebrate progress.
* Maintain a flexible schedule, including evenings and weekends, to meet program and organizational needs.


**Additional Responsibilities**


* Take on other duties as assigned to support the YMCA’s mission and evolving priorities.
* Completion of all required annual trainings related to safety, compliance, and child protection as assigned.

  


**PROGRAM SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES:**

  

* Lead and support high\-quality youth programs—including before/after school, track out, summer day camp, and outreach—that emphasize safety, relationships, skill\-building, character growth, and fun.
* Implement program enhancements and initiatives to improve quality and engagement.
* Oversee daily operations and programs in adherence to YMCA Standard Operating Procedures.
* Build and maintain collaborative relationships with schools, families, and community organizations.
* Obtain and maintain required certifications within 30 days of hire: CPRO, Basic First Aid, Administering Emergency Oxygen, and Emergency Medication Administration Training (EMAT).

  

**QUALIFICATIONS:**


* Degree in related field preferred and 1\+ year of related experience.
* Passion for building community and fostering meaningful relationships through programs and services.
* Experience supporting program delivery and staff development in a team\-based environment.
* Ability to coordinate staff, programs, and schedules effectively in a dynamic setting.
* Strong communication skills, including written, verbal, and public\-facing interactions.
* Demonstrates initiative, sound judgment, and strong organizational and time\-management skills.
* Builds inclusive, mission\-driven relationships with youth, families, and community members from diverse backgrounds.
* Bilingual or multilingual skills preferred, but not required.

  

**WORK ENVIRONMENT \& PHYSICAL DEMANDS:**



The physical demands described here represent those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.


* Primarily office and program settings with frequent interaction in gyms, classrooms, and outdoor spaces.
* Moderate noise levels; may be louder during youth or community activities.
* Regular use of computer, phone, and other office technology.
* Frequent standing, walking, bending, and reaching; occasional lifting or moving up to 40 lbs.
* Some work performed outdoors in varying weather conditions.
* Flexible schedule required — may include early mornings, evenings, weekends, and occasional travel between branches or sites.
* Must be able to provide valid identification for employment eligibility verification.
* Must possess a valid driver’s license and have access to reliable transportation.
* A clean driving record is required to meet YMCA insurance standards.
* Travel between branch and/or site locations, and to off\-site meetings and events is required.
* Must reside in the YMCA of the Triangle service area (Raleigh\-Durham\-Chapel Hill and surrounding areas).
* This position is 100% in person, with the flexibility to work at various branches and program locations across the YMCA of the Triangle as needed.
* Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential job functions.

  


**Salary \& Benefits**

This is a full\-time exempt position with a salary starting at $43,888, commensurate with experience and qualifications. The YMCA of the Triangle offers a generous benefits package including medical, dental and vision insurance; paid time off; an annual YMCA membership; and participation in the YMCA Retirement Fund, including a 12% employer contribution once eligibility requirements are met.

**Job Description:**


Brown University seeks a visionary, strategic, and deeply collaborative leader to serve as the next Executive Director of the Lizzie and Jonathan Tisch Center for Career Exploration and Associate Dean of the College. This is a defining opportunity to contribute to Brown’s Open Curriculum, a distinctive model of undergraduate education. At Brown, the Open Curriculum empowers students to become the architects of their own academic journeys. Career exploration is not a transactional postscript, but an essential extension of the power of a liberal arts education. As technological change, evolving workforce expectations, and artificial intelligence fundamentally reshape the global economy, Brown seeks an inspiring leader who can help students connect the core values of a Brown education with lifelong curiosity and a drive for ongoing purpose and usefulness.

  

The Executive Director and Associate Dean will lead the nationally recognized Tisch Center for Career Exploration, serve as a key member of the College's senior leadership team, and directly advise undergraduate students. This rare alignment of responsibilities reflects Brown's holistic approach to undergraduate education, intentionally integrating career exploration, academic advising, and student development. The successful candidate will embrace the promise and complexity of supporting self\-directed learners, positioning Brown as the national model for how liberal arts institutions prepare graduates for lives of purpose, leadership, and meaning in a rapidly evolving world.

  

The Executive Director and Associate Dean provides leadership, strategic direction, and high\-level oversight to a best\-in\-class career services and education center. The Executive Director leads University efforts to integrate career exploration and learning into all aspects of Brown’s undergraduate experience, serves as a member of the College’s senior leadership team, and is an important advocate and University ambassador for innovation in higher education career exploration. The Executive Director reports to the Dean of the College.

  

The Executive Director is expected to champion a culture of evidence\-based practice and continuous improvement. The ideal candidate will leverage modern data analytics to evaluate programs, demonstrate institutional value, anticipate employment trends, and ensure that all career development initiatives align with broader strategic enrollment, retention, and student success goals.
